input.strategy_title: Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag
input.strategy_markdown:
## Summary

RHOAI must provide a default vector store that is available out-of-the-box — without manual setup — so that Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag continue to function when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution image. Today these capabilities depend on an inline vector store provider bundled within the Llama Stack process; removing it (per RHAISTRAT-7474) will break them unless an alternative is available at the platform level.

## Problem Statement

Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag currently rely on an inline Milvus provider embedded in the Llama Stack distribution image to store and retrieve vector embeddings. This inline provider runs inside the Llama Stack process itself.

RHAISTRAT-7474 proposes removing inline providers from the Llama Stack distribution to improve GA readiness — shipping only what can be tested and maintained at scale, and aligning with Llama Stack's primary use case as a remote API server. However, no platform-level alternative exists today. If inline providers are removed without a replacement, any RHOAI user relying on Gen AI Studio's RAG capabilities or Auto Rag will lose functionality entirely — there is no workaround short of manually provisioning and configuring an external vector database.

Users expect vector storage to "just work" when they use Gen AI Studio or Auto Rag. The current out-of-the-box experience must be preserved even as the underlying architecture evolves.

## Affected Customers

* All RHOAI customers using Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
* All RHOAI customers using Auto Rag
* This is a platform-level product dependency: these features cannot function without a vector store

## Business Justification

* **Product integrity:** Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag are GA-track capabilities in RHOAI. Removing the inline vector store without a replacement breaks shipped product functionality for every user of these features.
* **Blocking dependency:** RHAISTRAT-7474 (removing inline providers for GA readiness) cannot proceed until this RFE is resolved. Silas Brenmark (Gen AI Studio lead) has identified this as a blocker.
* **User experience:** RHOAI differentiates on integrated, opinionated defaults. Requiring users to manually provision and configure a vector database before they can use the playground or Auto Rag degrades the out-of-the-box experience that customers expect from the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] A default vector store is available out-of-the-box on RHOAI without requiring users to manually provision or configure external infrastructure
* \[ \] Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] Auto Rag functions with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] The default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the Llama Stack instance (not an inline provider)
* \[ \] The default vector store is scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments (e.g., per-namespace isolation)
* \[ \] The default vector store is lightweight enough to run in resource-constrained environments without imposing significant overhead

## Success Criteria

* Users of Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag experience no functional regression when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution
* No additional manual setup steps are required for RAG workflows compared to the current experience
* RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and can proceed to implementation

## Open Questions

* What is the preferred scoping model — per namespace, per Llama Stack instance, or both? (Silas noted per-namespace is preferred for isolation, but Auto Rag may need per-instance scoping)
* Should users have a migration path from the default vector store to a production-grade vector database? (Bram Sundqvist raised the importance of aligning with commonly-used vector DB providers for easier migration)

## Strategy (AI Generated by Agentic SDLC Pipeline)

> **Note:** The full strategy exceeds Jira's description size limit and is stored as an attachment: `RHAISTRAT-8004-strategy.md`.

## Staff Engineer Input

**Correction 1 — OGX does not auto-provision PostgreSQL.** OGX defaults to SQLite for storage (`storage.kv.type: sqlite`, `storage.sql.type: sqlite` in the OGXServer CRD). The odh-dashboard gen-ai BFF hardcodes SQLite when creating OGXServer instances for the playground (`kv_sqlite` and `sql_sqlite` in `llamastack_config.go`). PostgreSQL is a supported backend but must be user-configured with an explicit `connectionString` secret. The strategy's claim that "every LlamaStackDistribution instance requires a PostgreSQL database" is incorrect — introducing PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension of existing infrastructure.

**Correction 2 — A Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector already exists.** The `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` image includes pgvector out of the box — confirmed in the [sclorg/postgresql-container Dockerfile](https://github.com/sclorg/postgresql-container/blob/master/16/Dockerfile.rhel9) (`INSTALL_PKGS="$INSTALL_PKGS pgvector"`). PostgreSQL 18 (RHEL 9) also includes pgvector. Furthermore, the model-registry-operator already uses `postgresql-16` as its auto-provisioned database image, and `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` is already present in the rhods-operator CSV for disconnected installs. No custom image build is needed. No Konflux onboarding is needed. The 1-2 sprint image onboarding estimate in the strategy can be eliminated.

**Architectural direction — platform-level database vs. self-provisioned.** Multiple RHOAI components now need PostgreSQL (model-registry, MLflow, and now OGX for pgvector). The preferred long-term direction is a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC, where each component consumes a connection string rather than self-provisioning. A shared platform-provided PostgreSQL via DSC will not be available until RHOAI 3.6. For 3.5, Gen AI Studio must provision its own PostgreSQL instance.

**Operator dependency for self-provisioning (RHAISTRAT-7164).** Self-provisioning PostgreSQL following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) would provide this operator layer. This is a hard dependency — until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers, there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. It will be challenging to commit this strategy to a specific release until that dependency is delivered.

**Fallback if RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time.** If the dashboard modularization is not ready for 3.5, the fallback is to require customers to bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Playground. Users would manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their PostgreSQL connection details. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the Playground largely abstracts OGX from users. The development team should define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of sprint planning.

**Decouple from Auto Rag.** Auto Rag integration with Gen AI Studio (RHAISTRAT-7824) is targeting RHOAI 3.6. This strategy should validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows. Auto Rag compatibility with pgvector will be addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824's scope. Remove Auto Rag from affected components, impacted teams, acceptance criteria, and validation requirements.

**Performance and index thresholds — dev experimentation scope.** The default pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation, not production usage. Strict latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) are not required. The sprint 1 benchmark should capture the inline Milvus baseline and verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude, not meet a specific threshold. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets — flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default. Users with production-scale vector workloads should use an external vector database. Remove open questions about latency thresholds, corpus size ranges, and index type selection.

**PostgreSQL resource sizing.** Reference the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource requests/limits as the starting point. Adjust based on sprint 1 benchmarking if needed.

**Alternative fallback — BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning.** If RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, an alternative to requiring customers to bring their own PostgreSQL is to have the gen-ai BFF provision the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails infrastructure. The BFF would create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured, if one does not already exist in the namespace. Caveats: (1) the implementation must be designed for portability — when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (3.6), the BFF should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning; (2) lifecycle management of the PostgreSQL instance must be carefully considered — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention.

**Existing remote vector store implementation is reusable.** Per the engineering team, the existing remote vector store implementation can be largely reused for pgvector integration. The majority of the work effort is around infrastructure and provisioning of the PostgreSQL/pgvector database, not the vector_io provider integration itself.

**Correction 3 — Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations.** The OGX vector_io provider configuration (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is completely separate from OGX's application storage backend configuration (`storage.kv.type`, `storage.sql.type`). This strategy only needs to configure the pgvector vector_io provider — it does not change the application storage backend, which remains on its existing default (SQLite). There is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because the application storage is not being touched. Remove any references to consolidating vector and application storage in a single database, and remove any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL upgrade path considerations.

# Operator-managed PostgreSQL provisioning for the Gen AI Studio default vector store

## Description

Implements operator-managed provisioning of the default vector store: the
RHOAI-controlled Gen AI Studio operator layer (delivered by the dashboard
operator modularization, RHAISTRAT-7164) manages the full PostgreSQL/pgvector
lifecycle per namespace, following the model-registry-operator
auto-provisioning pattern. Uses the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 image, which
includes pgvector out of the box — no custom image build and no pipeline
onboarding. This branch executes if the provisioning go/no-go decision selects
operator-managed provisioning (the dashboard operator modularization lands in
time for the target release).

## Scope

- Implement per-namespace PostgreSQL/pgvector provisioning in the RHOAI-controlled
  Gen AI Studio operator layer, following the model-registry-operator pattern:
  Deployment, Service, credentials secret, and storage, owned and reconciled by
  the operator.
- Generate and manage database credentials; clean up the provisioned instance on
  deletion of the owning resource.
- Set resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator
  PostgreSQL reference values, adjusted per the benchmark findings.
- Reference the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 image (pgvector included) through
  the related-image environment variable pattern so disconnected installs work.
- Validate end-to-end playground RAG workflows with the operator-provisioned
  default vector store (with the pgvector provider integration and the
  backend-for-frontend provider wiring in place).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Creating or configuring a playground with RAG in a namespace results in a
  PostgreSQL/pgvector instance provisioned and managed by the operator, with no
  manual user setup of external infrastructure.
- Provisioning uses the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 image (pgvector included)
  via the related-image reference pattern — no custom image build is introduced.
- Resource requests/limits for the provisioned instance start from the
  model-registry-operator reference values, adjusted per the benchmark findings
  when available.
- Deleting the owning resource cleans up the provisioned PostgreSQL instance and
  its credentials.
- End-to-end Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function out-of-the-box with
  the operator-provisioned default vector store, with no loss of current
  capability.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning).
- AC-2 (playground RAG workflows function with no loss of current capability).
- AC-4 (vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the OGX
  instance).
- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping — per-namespace isolation).
- AC-6 (lightweight enough for resource-constrained environments).

# BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning for the Gen AI Studio default vector store

## Description

Implements backend-managed provisioning of the default vector store: the gen-ai
backend-for-frontend provisions the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly —
creating the Deployment, Service, persistent storage, and credentials secret
when a playground with RAG is configured and no instance already exists in the
namespace — mirroring how the backend currently provisions guardrails
infrastructure. Because the backend is not an operator with a reconciliation
loop, lifecycle management (cleanup on playground deletion, pod-restart
resilience, credential rotation) receives explicit design attention. The design
is portable: when a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL becomes available in a
later release, the backend consumes the shared connection string instead of
self-provisioning. This branch executes if the provisioning go/no-go decision
selects BFF-managed provisioning.

## Scope

- Implement idempotent provisioning logic in the gen-ai backend-for-frontend:
  create the PostgreSQL/pgvector Deployment, Service, persistent volume claim,
  and credentials secret in the playground namespace only when a playground
  with RAG is configured and no suitable instance exists.
- Implement cleanup of the provisioned resources on playground deletion.
- Design and implement handling for pod restarts and credential rotation
  without an operator reconciliation loop.
- Structure connection consumption for portability: consume a connection secret
  reference that can later point at a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL
  instead of a self-provisioned instance.
- Use the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL 16 image (pgvector included) — no custom
  image build.
- Set resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator
  PostgreSQL reference values, adjusted per the benchmark findings.
- Validate end-to-end playground RAG workflows with the BFF-provisioned default
  vector store (with the pgvector provider integration and the
  backend-for-frontend provider wiring in place).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Configuring a playground with RAG in a namespace where no suitable PostgreSQL
  instance exists results in the backend-for-frontend creating the
  PostgreSQL/pgvector Deployment, Service, persistent storage, and credentials
  secret, with no manual user setup of external infrastructure.
- Deleting the playground cleans up the backend-provisioned PostgreSQL
  resources.
- Handling for pod restarts and credential rotation without a reconciliation
  loop is designed, documented, and implemented.
- The connection-consumption path is portable: the backend can consume a
  platform-provided shared connection string instead of self-provisioning when
  one becomes available.
- End-to-end Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function out-of-the-box with
  the BFF-provisioned default vector store, with no loss of current capability.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning).
- AC-2 (playground RAG workflows function with no loss of current capability).
- AC-4 (vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the OGX
  instance).
- AC-5 (multi-tenant scoping — per-namespace isolation).
- AC-6 (lightweight enough for resource-constrained environments).

# Bring-your-own PostgreSQL support for Gen AI Studio playground RAG

## Description

Implements the bring-your-own fallback for the default vector store: customers
provide their own PostgreSQL (with pgvector) by configuring the OGXServer custom
resource spec with their PostgreSQL connection details, and the playground
consumes that instance for RAG. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced
in OGX 1.0 and accepts a degraded out-of-the-box experience as the recorded
fallback: RAG capabilities in the Playground require user-provided PostgreSQL
under this approach. Users with production-scale vector workloads use an
external vector database in any case. This branch executes if the provisioning
go/no-go decision selects the bring-your-own fallback (neither operator-managed
nor BFF-managed provisioning is viable for the target release).

## Scope

- Validate the OGXServer custom resource connection-configuration path for
  user-provided PostgreSQL: secret-backed connection details consumed by the
  pgvector vector_io provider.
- Verify the playground RAG workflow functions end-to-end with a user-provided
  pgvector instance (with the pgvector provider integration and the
  backend-for-frontend provider wiring in place).
- Document the required customer configuration steps for bringing their own
  PostgreSQL (incidental reference documentation falling out of this change —
  no separate content work).
- Record and communicate the out-of-the-box degradation: no silent failures
  when RAG is used without a configured database.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user-configured OGXServer custom resource with PostgreSQL connection
  details (secret-backed) results in playground RAG workflows functioning
  against the user-provided pgvector instance.
- The required configuration steps for bringing their own PostgreSQL are
  documented for customers.
- Behavior when RAG is invoked without a configured database is explicit and
  communicated (clear error/guidance, no silent failure).
- The trade-off is recorded in the go/no-go decision record: this approach does
  not satisfy the out-of-the-box requirement and is accepted as fallback only.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-2 (playground RAG workflows function with the vector store, no loss of
  current capability for users who provide a database).
- AC-4 (vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the OGX
  instance).
- AC-1 (out-of-the-box availability) is explicitly NOT satisfied under this
  fallback — recorded in the decision record and the decomposition summary.

# Provisioning approach go/no-go for the RHOAI 3.5 default vector store

## Description

Resolves which PostgreSQL provisioning approach ships the default vector store
for Gen AI Studio playground RAG in RHOAI 3.5. Three bounded outcomes:
operator-managed provisioning in the RHOAI-controlled Gen AI Studio operator
layer delivered by the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164);
BFF-managed self-provisioning by the gen-ai backend-for-frontend; or requiring
customers to bring their own PostgreSQL. Operator-managed provisioning has a
hard dependency on RHAISTRAT-7164, whose delivery timing is uncertain — this
epic runs the go/no-go gate that the development team is to define as part of
sprint planning, and records the decision that selects which provisioning
implementation proceeds.

## Scope

- Define the go/no-go criteria and decision date for the provisioning approach
  (based on RHAISTRAT-7164 delivery status for the target release).
- Assess the delivery status of the dashboard operator modularization
  (RHAISTRAT-7164) against those criteria.
- Evaluate the BFF-managed provisioning alternative (including its lifecycle
  risks: no reconciliation loop, cleanup on playground deletion, pod restarts,
  credential rotation) against the bring-your-own PostgreSQL fallback.
- Record the decision (decision record / ADR) naming the selected approach, the
  evidence used, and the fallback if the selected approach fails late.
- Communicate the decision to the Gen AI Studio team and point the downstream
  plan at the selected implementation path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision record exists that names the selected provisioning approach for
  RHOAI 3.5, with explicit go/no-go criteria, the decision date, and the
  RHAISTRAT-7164 delivery-status evidence used.
- The decision record names the fallback approach if the selected one fails
  late (bring-your-own PostgreSQL or BFF-managed provisioning, as applicable).
- The decision is recorded and socialized with the Gen AI Studio team before
  the sprint in which the provisioning implementation starts.

## HLR Traceability

# Wire Gen AI Studio playground RAG to the pgvector vector_io provider

## Description

The gen-ai backend-for-frontend configures OGXServer instances for the
playground so that RAG workflows use the remote pgvector vector_io provider,
consuming connection details from a Kubernetes secret reference regardless of
who provisioned the database (platform operator, backend self-provisioning, or
user-supplied configuration). This keeps the wiring independent of the
provisioning decision and reusable when a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL
becomes available in a later release. Application storage configuration is
unchanged.

## Scope

- Extend the gen-ai backend-for-frontend's OGXServer instance creation to set
  the remote pgvector vector_io provider configuration (provider activation
  setting and connection secret reference) when playground RAG is enabled.
- Keep the existing application-storage settings emitted for OGXServer
  instances unchanged (existing SQLite default).
- Use standard OGX vector_io provider settings so the connection can later be
  redirected to an externally managed vector database without backend changes
  (migration path to production-grade vector databases).
- Validate the end-to-end playground RAG workflow (document ingestion,
  embedding, retrieval) against a pgvector-backed OGX instance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- OGXServer instances created for playgrounds with RAG enabled carry the remote
  pgvector vector_io provider configuration referencing a connection secret.
- The end-to-end playground RAG workflow (document ingestion, embedding,
  retrieval) functions against a pgvector-backed OGX instance with no manual
  vector-store setup steps in the user flow.
- Application-storage settings emitted by the backend-for-frontend are
  unchanged from current behavior.
- The provider configuration uses standard OGX vector_io settings, so the
  connection can be redirected to an external vector database without
  backend-for-frontend code changes.
- Rollback/feature flag: with the remote pgvector vector_io provider
  configuration unset or reverted (env-guarded provider activation path),
  playground RAG falls back to the previous provider behavior — the inline
  provider continues to serve RAG workflows during the transition window
  before inline providers are removed.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-1 (default vector store available out-of-the-box, no manual provisioning
  or configuration of external infrastructure).
- AC-2 (Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector
  store, no loss of current capability).

# Benchmark pgvector against the inline Milvus baseline and finalize default resource sizing

## Description

Produces the sprint-1 benchmark and sizing deliverable for the default vector
store: captures the inline Milvus baseline for representative playground RAG
vector operations, verifies that pgvector performs in the same order of
magnitude (dev-experimentation scope — no latency SLA thresholds), and
finalizes PostgreSQL resource requests/limits for the default instance,
starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL reference values. The
default pgvector instance targets development experimentation; users with
production-scale vector workloads are directed to an external vector database.

## Scope

- Build a benchmark harness/runbook covering representative playground RAG
  vector operations (embedding insert and similarity query) at typical
  playground document-set sizes.
- Capture the inline Milvus baseline for those operations (before inline
  providers are removed from the distribution).
- Run the same operations against the pgvector provider with the default flat
  scan (no index) configuration and compare orders of magnitude.
- Document a resource sizing recommendation for the default PostgreSQL/pgvector
  instance, starting from the model-registry-operator PostgreSQL
  requests/limits, and state whether flat scan remains adequate for typical
  playground document sets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A benchmark report captures the inline Milvus baseline for the representative
  playground RAG vector operations.
- The pgvector results (flat scan, no index) are within the same order of
  magnitude as the inline Milvus baseline for those operations.
- A resource sizing recommendation for the default PostgreSQL/pgvector instance
  is documented, starting from the model-registry-operator PostgreSQL
  requests/limits.
- The report states whether flat scan (no index) remains adequate for typical
  playground document-set sizes, with a recommendation if adjustment is needed.

## HLR Traceability

- AC-6 (default vector store lightweight enough for resource-constrained
  environments without significant overhead).
- AC-2 (no loss of current capability — measured as order-of-magnitude parity
  with the inline Milvus baseline per Staff Engineer Input).
